reason: Planting the lettuce directly addresses the early-crop goal, and the irrigated troughs are ready for seeds.
expectation: I expect the lettuce seeds to be planted in the shallow trough, though the result may require another step.

alternatives.reason: The potatoes also need planting, but the lettuce is the earlier crop.
The foil and fabric might make a cover for the tubers, but I want to plant the early crop first.

effect: The lettuce is sown and the early-crop goal is complete; it will need time to grow.
reaction: It is satisfying to have the first crop started, even though there is nothing to harvest yet.
reason: The seed potatoes need a growing bed, and the irrigated troughs are ready for them.
expectation: I expect to plant the potatoes in the deeper trough; they may still need a separate cover to keep light off the tubers.

alternatives.reason: The foil and fabric may make a tuber cover, but planting the potatoes first seems natural.

effect: The potatoes are planted beneath the granules, with shoots expected above and new tubers below; the light-protection goal remains.
reaction: The distinction between the shoots and developing tubers makes the deeper bed easier to picture.
reason: Foil and fabric are the only available combination, and they may make a cover to keep light off the tubers.
expectation: I expect a cover or covering material, though it may take another step to fit it to the trough.

effect: The foil and fabric made an opaque cover with an open top for the shoots, ready to fit over the potato bed.
reaction: The open top makes the cover’s purpose clear: shield the tubers while letting the shoots grow.
reason: Fitting the cover to the planted potato trough is the only available combination and should address the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the cover to keep light off the developing tubers while leaving room for the shoots.

effect: The cover completed the light-protection goal while leaving the shoots exposed and the bed able to drain and breathe.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the cover accommodate both the tubers and shoots.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and fitting the cover was most worthwhile: its open top and shaded root space showed how the shoots and developing tubers have different needs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the finished cover was a predictable final step, though it brought the construction to a satisfying close.

surprise.text: I had not initially pictured a cover that kept the root space dark while leaving the shoots in the light.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the planting and cover had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, partly to see how the crops develop and whether the promised harvests become part of the story.
